howBytesWereMeasured.pixels: pdftoppm -r 300 -gray writing binary P5 PGM DIRECTLY, one page at a time, each raster deleted as soon as it was measured (this container had 2.7 GB free). `-gray -png` was never used: it emits an RGB PNG that a naive grayscale reader misreads silently. The P5 reader was written for this lane and REFUSES any file whose magic is not P5, whose maxval is not 255, or whose raster is short, so a format substitution cannot pass unnoticed. Ink is grey < 128 of 255. Pinned sources were rendered WITH annotations (pdftoppm's default; -hide-annotations was used only in the one annotation experiment named below).
howBytesWereMeasured.differential: added = pixels inked on the delivered page and not on the paired pinned source page at the same coordinate; lost = the reverse. numpy boolean masks over the full 2550x3300 raster. The Indiana family binds no source binary, so its differential is canonical against boundary.
howBytesWereMeasured.rectBracketing: PUBLISHED IN BOTH CONVENTIONS. Per-control write and selection readings use rounded edges; refusal rects and the outside-every-rect scans use floor on the low edge and ceil on the high edge, which is the convention that can only OVER-count ink inside a box and under-count ink outside it. On ar-felony-seal-set the two conventions agree to the pixel on every one of the eleven selection controls.
howBytesWereMeasured.widgetRectangles: Read first-hand from each pinned binary with pdf-lib -- getForm().getFields(), acroField.getWidgets(), each widget's own /Rect and its /P page reference -- never taken from the family's own field map. The 50 ar-felony-seal-set refusals, which the map gives no rect at all, were resolved by field name against the source AcroForm this way: 50 of 50 resolved, 0 unmatched.
howBytesWereMeasured.flattenedAppearances: Each delivered page's /Resources /XObject dictionary walked with pdf-lib, every name matching /FlatWidget/i decompressed with decodePDFRawStream. An appearance counts as INKED when its stream carries Tj or TJ AND a show-text operand holds a non-whitespace character -- counting BOTH literal-string and HEX-string operands. That second half matters and this lane got it wrong first: the paragraph 8 mark on the ACIC petition is drawn as `<58> Tj`, and a detector reading only `(...)` operands returns 36 as 0.
howBytesWereMeasured.textAndQuotations: pdftotext in three modes -- -layout, -raw and default reading order -- because the default order fuses and splits words differently from -raw. A quoted printed line counts as verified if it matches under any of the three. Word geometry from pdftotext -bbox.
howBytesWereMeasured.digests: sha256sum on the files on disk, and `stat -c%s` for byte lengths. Nothing transcribed from a report.
howBytesWereMeasured.recordAnchors: Node script written for this lane: keys sorted recursively, JSON.stringify with no spacing, UTF-8 without ASCII escaping, then sha256 -- the JS mechanism the receipts name.
